caption: LUM-1336 CJK composer, A side: the pre-change binary at 60x24 lays a draft out one cell per *character*, so a wide glyph (2 terminal columns) shifts every following cell by one and ratatui's diff — which skips the cell after a wide symbol (`Buffer::diff` keeps `to_skip = symbol_width - 1`) — leaves the previous frame's cell on screen. Two glyphs render as `世C`; a 45-glyph draft (90 columns) renders as a single row showing only its first glyph plus that stale cell, i.e. the draft past the first character is invisible.

panels.label: 2. control: 40 half-width characters stay on one row

probe.why: half-width characters are one column each, which is why the defect needs wide glyphs to show up

panels.label: 3. two wide glyphs: the cell after 世 is left as the previous frame's `C` (the diff skipped it)

probe.why: the stale cell the pre-change build leaves behind
the second glyph is never painted: its cell is skipped as 'covered' by the wide glyph before it

panels.label: 4. 45 wide glyphs (90 columns) do not wrap: the row shows the first glyph and a stale cell, the rest is off-screen

probe.why: one 45-cell row for a 90-column draft, with the stale cell from the previous frame

probe.why: no continuation row exists, so 91% of the draft is not on screen

probe.why: no caret is painted anywhere on the composer row
